# Pilot Detection Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: General / Process
Readiness Contract: evidence-v1

## Decision Record

| ID | Decision | Basis / evidence | Remaining uncertainty, consequence, and check | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Use the existing manual Friday review process for this pilot; no automation introduced | Decided — user: "use the manual process for this pilot" | None; scope is explicitly manual-only | resolved |
| D2 | Accept up to seven days of detection delay as a known tradeoff of the manual cadence | Decided — owner "explicitly accepts up to seven days of detection delay" | Delay could mean a missed alert sits unnoticed up to a week; checked by D4's post-two-Fridays inspection | accepted-uncertainty |
| D3 | Owner assigns herself responsibility for inspecting missed alerts | Decided — user: "assigned herself to inspect missed alerts" | None | resolved |
| D4 | Review of missed alerts occurs after two Fridays of the pilot | Decided — user: "review after two Fridays" | None; this is the concrete check for D2's accepted delay | resolved |
| D5 | Automation is explicitly declined for the pilot; checklist is the only deliverable | Decided — user: "declined automation for the pilot"; "Done means ... no automation is introduced" | None | resolved |

## Decision History

_No superseded decisions._

## Critique Reconciliation

_No critique submitted for this specification version._

## Problem Statement

The reporting team needs a written checklist for a pilot that continues using the existing manual Friday review as the sole detection mechanism, rather than building or introducing any automated tooling. The checklist must make explicit the accepted detection-delay tradeoff, who owns catching what the manual cadence misses, and when that catch-up review happens.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Observable acceptance criterion | Decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Checklist names the Friday review as the pilot's detection mechanism | Checklist contains a line item identifying the weekly Friday review as the process step used for detection | D1 |
| R2 | Checklist states the accepted seven-day detection delay | Checklist contains a line item stating a maximum detection delay of seven days is an accepted tradeoff for this pilot | D2 |
| R3 | Checklist names the owner responsible for inspecting missed alerts | Checklist contains a line item naming the owner as responsible for inspecting alerts that the Friday review may have missed | D3 |
| R4 | Checklist specifies the missed-alert review occurs after two Fridays | Checklist contains a line item stating the missed-alert inspection happens following the second Friday of the pilot | D4 |
| R5 | Checklist contains no automation or systems-change item | Checklist has zero line items proposing, requiring, or implying new tooling, scripts, alerts infrastructure, or systems changes | D5 |

## Constraints

- No systems changes of any kind for this pilot; manual process only (D1, D5).
- Detection delay ceiling of seven days is accepted, not to be treated as a defect to fix within this pilot (D2).

## Success Criteria

- All four required items (Friday review, seven-day accepted delay, owner assignment, two-Fridays review checkpoint) appear in the checklist.
- The checklist introduces no automation.

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests

- Read the finished checklist and confirm R1–R5 are each present as identifiable line items.

### Regression Checks

- Not applicable; this is a one-time document deliverable, not a running system.

### Failure Signals

- Checklist omits any of the four required items.
- Checklist includes any automated/tooling component, contradicting D5.

### Verification Methods

- Owner (self) reviews the drafted checklist against R1–R5 before treating the pilot documentation as complete.

### Feedback Loop Design

- After two Fridays, owner inspects any alerts missed by the manual process (D4), which serves as the real-world check on the accepted seven-day delay (D2).

### Known Blind Spots

- A detection delay up to seven days means some alerts may go unnoticed until the Friday review; this is an accepted, not resolved, risk (D2).

## Inputs

- Existing manual Friday review process (unchanged).

## Outputs

- The pilot checklist document containing R1–R5.

## Out of Scope

- Any automated detection tooling or systems changes (D5).
- Redesigning the Friday review process itself.

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide

- Exact wording/formatting of checklist line items, provided R1–R5 are satisfied.

### Executor Must Escalate

- Any request or apparent need to introduce automation or systems changes.

### Executor Must Not Change

- The manual-only nature of the pilot (D1, D5).
- The accepted seven-day delay tradeoff and its two-Fridays check (D2, D4).

## Current Interpretation

Produce a single checklist document for the pilot that records the manual Friday review as the detection method, documents the accepted seven-day delay, assigns the owner to inspect missed alerts, and schedules that inspection after two Fridays — with no automation introduced anywhere in the pilot.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives

- None identified; deliverable is a static checklist, not a classifier.

### Potential False Negatives

- A checklist missing one of R1–R5 could be mistaken for complete; mitigated by the explicit acceptance criteria per requirement.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

_None._

### Non-Blocking

_None; all elements of the deliverable are explicitly specified._

### Intentional

- The seven-day detection delay is an intentionally accepted limitation of the manual process (D2), not a gap to close within this pilot.

## Risks

- Missed alerts during the up-to-seven-day window before the Friday catch (accepted per D2, checked per D4).

## Stakeholders

- Owner: assigned responsibility for missed-alert inspection (D3).
- Reporting team: runs the existing Friday review (D1).
